confidence_notes: I based the food anchors on 2026 cost-of-living aggregates I found by web search (Expatica/Numbeo data from June 2026, Numbeo, CityCost, Whereandwhen). An inexpensive meal is about $20–22, a mid-range dinner for two about $85–89, a cappuccino about $5–5.20 and a domestic draft beer about $6. I added a small uplift because the pricing window is July 2026, when visitor-area prices are higher. Cocktail and wine prices come from my general knowledge and their usual ratio to beer in US mid-size tourist cities, not from a direct search. The accommodation prices are my own general estimates, not checked against live listings. Orlando has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel prices are especially uncertain. Hotel prices vary a lot between the theme-park and International Drive corridor and other areas, and July is peak family season. The exchange-rate figure came from a search summary that cited the RBA's published reading for 18 November 2026. I did not open the rba.gov.au page myself, so I could not confirm the figure directly there.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are similar to other large US Sun Belt tourist cities such as Tampa and Las Vegas, outside the Strip. The search results also showed Orlando restaurant and drink prices close to New York's and a little below Washington's. Accommodation reflects Orlando's large supply of motels and mid-range hotels.
